newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Summit to confirm IGC calendar - de Charette.
newsitem.headline: Summit to confirm IGC calendar - de Charette.

text.p: The European Union summit in Dublin on Saturday should allow leaders to confirm the intention to finish the inter-governmental conference (IGC) in June 1997, French Foreign Minister Herve de Charette said on Tuesday.
"Are we agreed that it should end in June in Amsterdam?" de Charette asked on the margins of the General Affairs Council. "I would hope that that timetable would be confirmed."
French President Jacques Chirac, supported by German Chancellor Helmut Kohl, asked for the Dublin summit to be held to give the IGC a push.
France argues that no substantial progress has so far been forthcoming, with each country just repeating its desires.
De Charette and German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel are to meet in Paris on Wednesday to discuss the Franco-German position on the IGC.
But de Charette said the two countries were unlikely to come up with something that they would present to their partners as a fait accompli.
"We thought that it was not very opportune vis a vis our colleagues to take a completed text to Dublin," de Charette told a news conference.
